item.title: Culture must be preserved for future generations
item.description: Papua New Guinea’s culture and traditions must be protected and passed on to young people as the country moves into its next 50 years, says Assistant Director of the Institute of Papua New Guinea Studies Dr Naomi Simet. Dr Simet said culture is important to Papua New Guinea’s identity, values and way of life.
item.content:encoded:
Papua New Guinea’s culture and traditions must be protected and passed on to young people as the country moves into its next 50 years, says Assistant Director of the Institute of Papua New Guinea Studies Dr Naomi Simet.

Dr Simet said culture is important to Papua New Guinea’s identity, values and way of life.

Speaking at Kopkop College’s 51st pre-Independence anniversary celebration in Port Moresby, she said traditional songs, dances, music, chants and costumes carry important knowledge from past generations.

“Our culture is very important. Primarily for our identity as a country. As a country moving into a lot of changes taking place globally and locally. So our culture gives us value. It gives us our ways of civilization which has to be respected and upheld.

"It should be the platform for our children to learn from in order to understand how they came and why is it important today and to also inform them of where they are going.” Dr Simet said.

Dr Simet said Papua New Guinea has a rich culture that has survived colonialism and other outside influences.

She said cultural practices have helped keep people connected to their identity and history.

Dr Simet, who has worked with the Institute of Papua New Guinea Studies since 2001, has spent about 25 years researching traditional dance and performing arts.

She said dance is also an important way for people to communicate ideas and express themselves.

“People don't really express themselves freely, but through performing arts they are able to come together, perform together, foster that appreciation and respect for one another,” Dr Simet said.

She said the different cultural performances at Kopkop College showed how diversity can bring Papua New Guineans together.

Students from different provinces performed traditional dances during the celebration.

Dr Simet said the performances showed that national unity can grow through respecting and preserving the country’s many cultures.

She also called on schools to help pass cultural knowledge to the next generation.

She said culture should not only remain in books or libraries, but must be taught and practised by students.

“We need to actually teach it to our students because they will enact it and they will take it on and they will use it to enable its continuity into the future,” she said.

Meanwhile, Dr Simet commended Dame Maria Kopkop and the college team for organising the celebration and promoting culture through education.

item.title: No Independence celebrations in Hagen town
item.description: Western Highlands will mark Papua New Guinea’s 51st Independence Day without a major provincial celebration. Governor Wai Rapa said the provincial government decided this after observing the way recent public events have been conducted.
item.content:encoded:
Western Highlands will mark Papua New Guinea’s 51st Independence Day without a major provincial celebration.

Governor Wai Rapa said the provincial government decided this after observing the way recent public events have been conducted.

Instead of bringing people together, some events have ended up in fights, that have caused a lot of destruction.

“We must ask ourselves, what is the real meaning of Independence? It is not about fighting, drinking, or destroying property. Independence is about our people, our freedom, and taking responsibility for our country.” Rapa said.

Governor Rapa stressed that youth are an important part of the country’s future, but they must understand that Independence Day is more than just a public celebration.

He added that the province wants the youth to start thinking about their role in building Western Highlands and Papua New Guinea.

“We want our young people to understand why we celebrate Independence. We want them to respect the country, respect each other, and think about what they can do for the future," Rapa added.

The Governor also said the decision does not mean Western Highlands will ignore Independence Day. People are free to mark the day peacefully in their own communities, churches, homes, and families. But there will be no major provincial government-hosted celebration.

While canceling the provincial celebrations, Governor Rapa reiterated that it's also a time for the province to look at how future public events can be organised in a more peaceful and meaningful way.

“Celebration must not become an excuse for violence. If we cannot celebrate peacefully, then we have to step back and think about what we are doing," he said.

The Western Highlands Governor has also called on parents, community leaders, the churches, and the youth to take responsibility for keeping the communities peaceful.

He said Independence Day should be a time to appreciate the freedom Papua New Guineans have and to think about the work still needed to improve the country.

An Independence Day dawn service at 6am this morning was hosted by members of the Royal Papua New Guinea Constabulary [RPNGC] and Governor Rapa at Independence Hill.

item.title: Australia sends Independence wishes to PNG
item.description: Australia has congratulated Papua New Guinea on its 51st Independence anniversary, with a special message to the people of Morobe Province and Lae. Australian Consul-General in Lae, Brenton Kanowski, extended the message on behalf of the Australian Government, describing Lae as a community he is proud to call home.
item.content:encoded:
Australia has congratulated Papua New Guinea on its 51st Independence anniversary, with a special message to the people of Morobe Province and Lae.

Australian Consul-General in Lae, Brenton Kanowski, extended the message on behalf of the Australian Government, describing Lae as a community he is proud to call home.

Kanowski praised the resilience, warmth and strong sense of community among the people of Morobe and Lae.

He also highlighted the close relationship between Australia and Papua New Guinea, saying the two countries share a unique and enduring friendship built on their common history.

“Today, we are more than just neighbours or friends – we are allies,” Kanowski said.

He wished the people of Papua New Guinea a happy Independence Day as the country marks 51 years since gaining independence from Australia.

item.title: Schools arrive for Lae Independence ceremony
item.description: School children have arrived for the 51st Independence Day state ceremony in Lae this morning. The students are among groups taking part in the official programme at the stadium, where they are expected to march and take their positions ahead of the main ceremony.
item.content:encoded:
School children have arrived for the 51st Independence Day state ceremony in Lae this morning.

The students are among groups taking part in the official programme at the stadium, where they are expected to march and take their positions ahead of the main ceremony.

According to the programme, schools were scheduled to arrive from 7.30am, with VIPs and dignitaries arriving from 8am.

The Guard of Honour will prepare before the arrival of the parade host, Colonel Michael Percy Marai, at 9am.

Morobe Governor and Finschhafen MP Renbo Paita is scheduled to arrive at 9.05am, followed by Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Lands and Physical Planning John Rosso at 9.10am.

The national Independence Day celebrations are being held today, September 16, marking 51 years since Papua New Guinea gained independence in 1975.

item.title: Chief supt. Beli assumes command of Eastern Highlands police
item.description: Residents of Eastern Highlands Province turned out in large numbers on Monday to welcome incoming Provincial Police Commander, Chief Superintendent Albert Beli. Police officers staged a ceremonial parade along the main thoroughfare outside the police station in the heart of Goroka town, drawing a massive crowd of locals who gathered to witness the handover.
item.content:encoded:
Residents of Eastern Highlands Province turned out in large numbers on Monday to welcome incoming Provincial Police Commander, Chief Superintendent Albert Beli.

Police officers staged a ceremonial parade along the main thoroughfare outside the police station in the heart of Goroka town, drawing a massive crowd of locals who gathered to witness the handover.

Addressing the officers and the public, Chief Supt. Beli expressed gratitude for his appointment and pledged to prioritize law and order across the province.

"We have a duty to perform, and we must work with pride, standing tall and strong for the people of this province and the country as a whole," Beli said.

He urged police personnel to maintain professional standards, asking them to continue working cohesively and serving the community with respect.

Beli also appealed directly to the public for cooperation, emphasizing that community partnership is vital for crime prevention and public safety.

"Together, with the support of the community, we can create a safe and peaceful environment for everyone to live in," he said.

item.title: Vanimo catholic youths mark independence with faith and purpose
item.description: As Papua New Guinea marks its 51st Independence anniversary, Catholic youths from the inland communities of the Vanimo Catholic Diocese are marking the occasion in a different but meaningful way, through faith, fellowship, culture and reflection. Young people from Wasengla, Maka, Utai, Fas, Kembi, Moi-Kasai and Yapsi are gathering at Utai Catholic Parish from September 14 to 18 for the 2026 Inland
item.content:encoded:
As Papua New Guinea marks its 51st Independence anniversary, Catholic youths from the inland communities of the Vanimo Catholic Diocese are marking the occasion in a different but meaningful way, through faith, fellowship, culture and reflection.

Young people from Wasengla, Maka, Utai, Fas, Kembi, Moi-Kasai and Yapsi are gathering at Utai Catholic Parish from September 14 to 18 for the 2026 Inland Denary Youth Rally.

Rather than making Independence celebrations only about entertainment, the youths are using the week to strengthen their faith, build friendships and discuss issues affecting young people and their communities.

The five-day program combines prayer, Holy Mass, catechesis, group discussions, sports, cultural activities, music, drama and youth fellowship.

A major focus of the morning conferences is on practical issues facing young people, including family life, marriage, drugs and alcohol, fighting and violence, leadership, personal dignity and the role of young people in the Church.

The program also provides space for the youths to express themselves through a traditional cultural show, Olympic-style games, Gospel action songs, drama, a composed hymn and other presentations. Spiritual activities including the Rosary, Confession, Holy Hour, Eucharistic prayer and youth blessings form an important part of the gathering.

The rally is being guided by the words of Jesus in Mark 8:36: “For what does it profit a man to gain the whole world, yet lose his soul?”

The message carries particular meaning during Independence celebrations, reminding young people that the future of Papua New Guinea is not only about economic progress and development, but also about the values, character and choices of its young generation.

For the inland youths, Independence week therefore becomes an opportunity to celebrate who they are, where they come from and the kind of Papua New Guinea they want to build.

Through the gathering, the young people are being encouraged to carry their faith beyond the parish, into their families, schools, villages and communities, where they can become positive examples and future leaders.

As PNG celebrates 51 years of nationhood, the youths at Utai are showing that Independence can also be celebrated through purpose, unity, culture and faith.

Their celebration is not simply about looking back at 51 years of independence, it is also about preparing themselves for the years ahead.

item.title: Firearms surrendered under ‘Make Hela Safe Again’ campaign
item.description: The voluntary illegal firearms surrender initiative in Hela is steadily gaining traction, signaling a powerful shift away from tribal hostilities and toward lasting peace. Governor Philip Undialu confirmed that another firearm was surrendered today.
item.content:encoded:
The voluntary illegal firearms surrender initiative in Hela is steadily gaining traction, signaling a powerful shift away from tribal hostilities and toward lasting peace.

Governor Philip Undialu confirmed that another firearm was surrendered today.

Tomorrow, September 16, Hela will celebrate the 51st Independence Day and also launch the Illegal Firearm Surrender Program.

"At exactly 12:00pm today, a fully loaded pistol along with 15 live rounds of ammunition was handed over to provincial officials. This latest act of good will raises the total number of weapons collected under the amnesty program to six, reducing the circulation of illicit arms," he said.

The handover comes on the heels of a significant breakthrough over the weekend. Last Saturday, local youths voluntarily relinquished two military-grade rifles; an AK-47 assault weapon and an SR8 tactical rifle. Their decision was widely praised as a courageous stand against the cycle of violence that has long plagued the province..

Governor Undialu stressed that earlier in the week, another young man personally delivered an M16 A2 service rifle to him.

He commended the young men for their bravery in rejecting violence and choosing a path of renewal. He emphasized that the campaign is not merely about collecting weapons but about nurturing opportunities for growth, reconciliation, and community development.

“The tide of positive change is rising across Hela,” he said, urging leaders, youth, and the people to sustain the momentum.

He reaffirmed that dismantling the culture of tribal warfare and eliminating illegal firearms are essential steps toward buildings a safer, more prosperous future for Hela Province and Papua New Guinea.

item.content:encoded:
‎‎Celebrations are well underway in Alotau, Milne Bay, as a three-day program began yesterday to commemorate Papua New Guinea's 51st Independence anniversary. ‎ ‎Activities started as early as eight in the morning and the excitement is building up across Alotau.

Government vehicles were seen convoying through the main streets of Alotau town in a spectacle of red, black and gold colors with cultural groups on board chanting, singing, dancing, and sharing the festive spirit with goodies shared to bystanders along the roadside. ‎ ‎With just hours remaining for PNG to celebrate its 51 years of being independent as a country, the convoy of vehicles held yesterday and today demonstrates unity and solidarity in the province. ‎ ‎It is also a call to citizens of Alotau town to come together as people of Milne Bay and celebrate on Wednesday, 16th of September. ‎ ‎Milne Bay Tourism Bureau has been tasked to organize and coordinate Alotau's celebrations.

The three-day program started with cultural dances, sports and live performance by King of Tolai Rock Leonard Kania and Basil Greg. ‎ ‎Similar activities will continue today leading up to the actual day tomorrow. ‎ ‎The celebrations in Alotau on Wednesday will include marching, led by Correctional Institute Services, followed by the Police Force, Provincial and private security services, Milne Bay Provincial Administration, scouts, schools, churches, non-government organisations, business houses and other interested groups. ‎ ‎The synchronized march will be provided by the famous Manus drum beat by Milne Bay Manus Cultural group. ‎ ‎Fun activities will also be featured on Wednesday including pikinini sports, greasy poles, catch-the-piglets among other fun games. ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎

item.title: National Fire Service station officially established in Tari
item.description: The National Fire Service now has a permanent station in Tari Town, Hela Province.

item.title: First PNG journalists partake in war training
item.description: Three Papua New Guinean journalists, including one from the National Broadcasting Corporation, are among twenty-five journalists from Asia and Turkey, undergoing an intensive 2-week War Journalism training workshop in Ankara, Turkey.
